title: Bild and The Telegraph Outline Possible Russian Moves Against NATO; Baltic and Nordic Leaders Push Back on Imminent-Attack Fears
detail: German tabloid Bild and the UK's The Telegraph reported August 31, 2026 detailed scenarios for how Russia could test NATO short of a full Article 5 invasion — including underwater infrastructure sabotage, a 'Narva scenario' of unmarked operatives stirring unrest in Estonia's border city, sudden deployment to Gotland or the Åland Islands, a manufactured Svalbard crisis, a push through the Suwałki Corridor, staged border incidents, false-flag use of captured Ukrainian drones, and cyberattacks designed to trigger Article 5 debate without a clear-cut military response. Polish PM Donald Tusk was cited warning the next seven to eight months 'could be critical' for European security, and the New York Times reported Putin is aiming for the 'collapse of NATO and the EU from within' in 2026. Baltic and Nordic officials pushed back the same day: Latvian PM Andris Kulbergs said 'readiness for a possible threat is not the same as an immediate threat — these two things must not be confused'; Finnish President Alexander Stubb told Bild he sees 'neither evidence nor facts' for near-term Russian aggression; Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna called ongoing Russian sabotage 'state-sponsored terrorism' rather than mere 'hybrid warfare'; and Romanian Defence Minister Radu Miruță said he does not believe 'Russia has any intention to attack a NATO member country.' Tusk struck a more cautious note, saying escalation from Russia's side is 'progressing.' The scenario reporting follows Bloomberg's August 28 account of European skepticism that CIA Director Ratcliffe's Moscow trip was primarily meant to deter a Baltic attack, and continues to test the credibility of US-backed Article 5 assurances amid the ongoing Pentagon force-posture review.

media.caption: Why the Baltics are pushing back against new fears of a Russian attack
